description: Safe serialization behavior, supported values, and intentional boundaries.

dos: Provide bounded, non-throwing representations for complex values, including Errors, functions, symbols, BigInts, buffers, cycles, and unserializable properties.
Replace up to 100 non-empty literal string entries from the optional secrets iterable in every serialized string value; ignore non-string entries.
Keep serialization limits separate from secrecy rules.
Represent unsupported non-plain objects using safely readable enumerable own properties; omit inherited, non-enumerable, accessor-backed, or hostile state.
Limit maxKeys to retained source data properties, including enumerable Error metadata; an over-limit object may contain one additional collision-safe [TRUNCATED] metadata property.
Serialize indexed array items only and omit enumerable named array properties.
Track cycles along the active recursion path so repeated non-cyclic references serialize independently and active-path references emit the circular marker.
Reduce unexpected hostile-value inspection errors to [UNSERIALIZABLE] at the public boundary.
Redact keys at the represented depth before truncating their child values beyond maxDepth.
Serialize Error name, message, stack, and enumerable data-property metadata at the Error's child depth, applying maxDepth consistently.
donts: Do not invoke getters, including enumerable accessors.
Do not count the optional truncation metadata slot as retained source data.
Do not let hostile diagnostic values make the public serializer throw.
Do not bypass maxDepth for Error metadata.
